:::{#exr-coordinates-practice}
#### Finding coordinates in a basis other than the indicator vectors

The [coordinates](#def-coordinates) of a vector depend on the [basis](#def-basis),
and they equal its entries only in the basis of [indicator vectors](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-indicator-vector).
The vectors $\vecf{a}_1 = \tp{(2, 0)}$ and $\vecf{a}_2 = \tp{(1, 1)}$ form a basis of $\reals^2$.
Let

$$
\vecf{x} = \sbmat{7 \\ 3}.
$$

Find the coordinates of $\vecf{x}$ in the basis $\vecf{a}_1, \vecf{a}_2$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Write $c_1 \vecf{a}_1 + c_2 \vecf{a}_2$ entry by entry,
and start from the second entry.

:::

:::
